import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Read the data
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 12))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# 1. Age distribution
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
current_year = 2014  # Based on the data
df['Age'] = current_year - df['Year_Birth']
ax1.hist(df['Age'], bins=20, color='skyblue', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax1.set_xlabel('Age')
ax1.set_ylabel('Frequency')
ax1.set_title('Customer Age Distribution')

# 2. Income distribution
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
ax2.hist(df['Income'].dropna(), bins=20, color='lightcoral', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax2.set_xlabel('Income')
ax2.set_ylabel('Frequency')
ax2.set_title('Income Distribution')

# 3. Education levels
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
education_counts = df['Education'].value_counts()
ax3.bar(education_counts.index, education_counts.values, color='lightgreen', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax3.set_xlabel('Education Level')
ax3.set_ylabel('Count')
ax3.set_title('Education Distribution')
ax3.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 4. Total spending by product category
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
spending_cols = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']
total_spending = df[spending_cols].sum()
categories = ['Wines', 'Fruits', 'Meat', 'Fish', 'Sweets', 'Gold']
ax4.bar(categories, total_spending.values, color='orange', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax4.set_xlabel('Product Category')
ax4.set_ylabel('Total Spending')
ax4.set_title('Total Spending by Product Category')
ax4.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 5. Purchase channels
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
purchase_cols = ['NumWebPurchases', 'NumCatalogPurchases', 'NumStorePurchases']
total_purchases = df[purchase_cols].sum()
channels = ['Web', 'Catalog', 'Store']
ax5.pie(total_purchases.values, labels=channels, autopct='%1.1f%%', startangle=90, colors=['#ff9999', '#66b3ff', '#99ff99'])
ax5.set_title('Purchase Distribution by Channel')

# 6. Marital status
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
marital_counts = df['Marital_Status'].value_counts()
ax6.bar(marital_counts.index, marital_counts.values, color='plum', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax6.set_xlabel('Marital Status')
ax6.set_ylabel('Count')
ax6.set_title('Marital Status Distribution')
ax6.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 7. Income vs Total Spending scatter plot
ax7 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
df['TotalSpending'] = df[spending_cols].sum(axis=1)
ax7.scatter(df['Income'], df['TotalSpending'], alpha=0.6, color='purple', edgecolor='black', s=50)
ax7.set_xlabel('Income')
ax7.set_ylabel('Total Spending')
ax7.set_title('Income vs Total Spending')

# 8. Number of children
ax8 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1])
df['TotalKids'] = df['Kidhome'] + df['Teenhome']
kids_counts = df['TotalKids'].value_counts().sort_index()
ax8.bar(kids_counts.index, kids_counts.values, color='cyan', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax8.set_xlabel('Number of Children')
ax8.set_ylabel('Count')
ax8.set_title('Household Children Distribution')

# 9. Campaign acceptance rate
ax9 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
campaign_cols = ['AcceptedCmp1', 'AcceptedCmp2', 'AcceptedCmp3', 'AcceptedCmp4', 'AcceptedCmp5', 'Response']
acceptance_rates = df[campaign_cols].mean() * 100
campaigns = ['Cmp1', 'Cmp2', 'Cmp3', 'Cmp4', 'Cmp5', 'Response']
ax9.bar(campaigns, acceptance_rates.values, color='gold', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax9.set_xlabel('Campaign')
ax9.set_ylabel('Acceptance Rate (%)')
ax9.set_title('Campaign Acceptance Rates')
ax9.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

plt.suptitle('Customer Marketing Campaign Analysis Dashboard', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.995)
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
